displayedInputs.question:
An insect lives on the surface of a regular tetrahedron with edges of length \(1.\) It wishes to travel on the surface of the tetrahedron from the midpoint of one edge to the midpoint of the opposite edge. What is the length of the shortest such trip? (Note: Two edges of a tetrahedron are opposite if they have no common endpoint.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

A point \(P\) is selected at random from the interior of the pentagon with vertices \(A = (0, 2),\) \(B = (4, 0),\) \(C = (2\pi + 1, 0),\) \(D = (2\pi + 1, 4),\) and \(E = (0, 4).\) What is the probability that \(\angle APB\) is obtuse?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

A circle centered at \(A\) with a radius of \(1\) and a circle centered at \(B\) with a radius of \(4\) are externally tangent. A third circle is tangent to the first two and to one of their common external tangents as shown. The radius of the third circle is

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

In rectangle \(ABCD,\) points \(F\) and \(G\) lie on \(\overline{AB}\) so that \(AF = FG = GB\) and \(E\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{DC}.\) Also, \(\overline{AC}\) intersects \(\overline{EF}\) at \(H\) and \(\overline{EG}\) at \(J.\) The area of rectangle \(ABCD\) is \(70.\) Find the area of triangle \(EHJ.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

In triangle \(ABC,\) \(\angle ABC = 45^\circ.\) Point \(D\) is on \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(2 \cdot BD = CD\) and \(\angle DAB = 15^\circ.\) Find \(\angle ACB.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Problems \(7,\) \(8,\) and \(9\) are about these kites.

To promote her school’s annual Kite Olympics, Genevieve makes a small kite and a large kite for a bulletin board display. The kites look like the one in the diagram. For her small kite Genevieve draws the kite on a one-inch grid. For the large kite she triples both the height and width of the entire grid.

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

What is the number of square inches in the area of the small kite?

A square piece of paper, \(4\) inches on a side, is folded in half vertically. Both layers are then cut in half parallel to the fold. Three new rectangles are formed, a large one and two small ones. What is the ratio of the perimeter of one of the small rectangles to the perimeter of the large rectangle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

Car \(M\) traveled at a constant speed for a given time. This is shown by the dashed line. Car \(N\) traveled at twice the speed for the same distance. If Car \(N\)’s speed and time are shown as a solid line, which graph illustrates this?
